\section[il risparmio]{il risparmio — the saving; savings}

\label{lesson:IT-C395-risparmio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the regular fee, then the Italian for the mortgage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il risparmio}
\textbf{il risparmio} — \textquotedblleft{}the saving; savings\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho usato i miei risparmi per il viaggio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I used my savings for the trip.}
\end{quote}

\emph{I risparmi} — your savings. Built on \emph{risparmiare}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{risparmio} is built on \emph{risparmiare} \textquotedblleft{}to save\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{ri-} and an older \emph{sparmiare}, a form of \emph{sparagnare}, which EtymDB traces to Frankish \emph{sparanjan} \textquotedblleft{}to spare\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il risparmio}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il risparmio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il risparmio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the regular fee, then the Italian for the mortgage, then say \emph{il risparmio} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il risparmio mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The saving; savings\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[l'investimento]{l'investimento — the investment}

\label{lesson:IT-C395-investimento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the mortgage, then the Italian for the saving.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'investimento}
\textbf{l'investimento} — \textquotedblleft{}the investment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Comprare casa è un buon investimento, se i prezzi salgono.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Buying a house is a good investment, if prices go up.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fare un investimento} — to make an investment.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{investimento} is built on \emph{investire}, from Latin \emph{investīre} \textquotedblleft{}to clothe, to cover\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{vestis} \textquotedblleft{}garment\textquotedblright{}; the money sense, putting money into something, came later.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'investimento}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'investimento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'investimento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the mortgage, then the Italian for the saving, then say \emph{l'investimento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'investimento mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The investment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[l'interesse]{l'interesse — the interest (on money); the interest}

\label{lesson:IT-C395-interesse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the saving, then the Italian for the investment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'interesse}
\textbf{l'interesse} — \textquotedblleft{}the interest (on money); the interest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se lasci i soldi in banca, prendi un piccolo interesse.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If you leave the money in the bank, you earn a little interest.}
\end{quote}

Also curiosity and advantage: \emph{nel tuo interesse} — in your interest.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{interesse} is the Latin verb \emph{interesse} \textquotedblleft{}to be between, to make a difference\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short) used as a noun; in Medieval Latin it meant the compensation owed on a loan. It is built from \emph{inter} and \emph{esse} \textquotedblleft{}to be\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'interesse}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the saving, then the Italian for the investment, then say \emph{l'interesse} again

\section[il tasso]{il tasso — the rate}

\label{lesson:IT-C395-tasso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the investment, then the Italian for the interest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il tasso}
\textbf{il tasso} — \textquotedblleft{}the rate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il tasso di interesse è del due per cento.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The interest rate is two per cent.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Il tasso di cambio} — the exchange rate. A different \emph{tasso} is the badger.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tasso} \textquotedblleft{}rate\textquotedblright{} is built on \emph{tassare} \textquotedblleft{}to assess\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{taxāre} \textquotedblleft{}to value, to assess\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short). The animal \emph{tasso} is a different word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[l'inflazione]{l'inflazione — the inflation}

\label{lesson:IT-C395-inflazione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the interest, then the Italian for the rate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'inflazione}
\textbf{l'inflazione} — \textquotedblleft{}the inflation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Con l'inflazione alta, i soldi valgono meno.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{With high inflation, money is worth less.}
\end{quote}

Literally a swelling: prices blow up.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{inflazione} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{īnflātiō} \textquotedblleft{}a blowing into, a swelling\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{īnflāre} \textquotedblleft{}to blow into\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{flāre} \textquotedblleft{}to blow\textquotedblright{}; the economic sense probably came through English.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
